extracted.intended_audience: research administrators, university sponsored programs officers, grant and contract managers, and scholars of research administration policy
extracted.subtask_description: Historical analysis and practical account of how OMB Circular A-110 was revised through the work of Joseph Warner's COGR subcommittee (1976–1979), highlighting the policy principles, interpretive standards, and implementation practices that guided university–federal sponsor relationships.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniform administrative requirements (one set of requirements)
rubrics_metrics.description: A-110 should provide one set of requirements for recipients rather than a multiplicity of different agency rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The subcommittee argued for uniform standards so institutions would not have to negotiate separately with each agency; uniformity simplifies administration and reduces burdens on universities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards must advance the public interest and be acceptable to institutions
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulatory standards should both advance the public interest and be acceptable to the institutions to which they apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Principles should be reasonable and implementable without major disruption or cost—balancing stewardship of public funds with practicability for academic institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimize paperwork and administrative costs; provide flexibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal principles should be standardized but not so prescriptive as to create unnecessary paperwork or costs for research administrators and faculty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The subcommittee promoted streamlining, clarification, and consolidation of cumbersome requirements so research administrators could focus on supporting research rather than excessive compliance tasks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit government rights regarding subrecipients and access to records
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions of 'subrecipient' and 'substantive work' should be narrow; government access to books, documents, papers, and records should be focused on material specific to the program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Yale's comments urged that subrecipients be public/private institutions receiving funds for cooperative projects (not vendors) and that audit/access rights not be overly broad, to reduce administrative burden and protect appropriate institutional boundaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separate timing for technical and financial reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Technical reports and financial reports need not be submitted simultaneously by award recipients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OMB clarified it did not intend simultaneous submission; campuses often use different offices for technical vs financial reports, making simultaneous submission impractical—agencies can obtain needed information from their counterparts if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Property vests with grantee; disposal rules for low-value items
rubrics_metrics.description: Property purchased under federal grants generally vests with the grantee; campuses may dispose of items under a specified unit-cost threshold without federal approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subcommittee advocated that items under a threshold (discussed early as $5,000) could be disposed of without agency approval; this principle underlies current practice of equipment remaining on campus to support future research/teaching.

rubrics_metrics.name: Increase equipment/non-expendable property threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: Raise the dollar threshold that defines non-expendable personal property (equipment) to reduce inventory and tracking burdens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The subcommittee recommended raising the threshold from $300 to $500 (and later practice moved to $5,000) and suggested a useful life criterion (two years) to align with Cost Accounting Standards Board guidance and reduce administrative cost.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow residual inventory to be used without reimbursing government
rubrics_metrics.description: Residual expendable personal property remaining at project closeout may be used by the institution without reimbursing the federal government unless an audit shows stockpiling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This recommendation reduced closeout paperwork and recognized that small leftover supplies are not worth the administrative cost of tracking and reimbursement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organize Attachment N: clear headings and property categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Property management standards (Attachment N) should segregate and identify sections clearly (Definitions, Real Property, Non-Expendable Property, Expendable Personal Property, Intangible Property).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clear organization and headings reduce confusion about which rules apply to different property types and help administrators comply more easily.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procurement standards: prevent unethical conduct but preserve fundraising and practical procurement practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Procurement provisions should establish ethical standards (no extortion or improper gratuities) while not precluding legitimate university fundraising or practical interactions with vendors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purchasing directors argued procurement rules should allow institutions to solicit gifts, permit interaction with potential contractors to develop specifications, and avoid wording that inhibits normal procurement/ fundraising activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow contractors who help develop specs to bid (with conditions)
rubrics_metrics.description: If contractors assist institutions in developing technical specifications, they should not automatically be barred from bidding for follow-on work where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DHEW was later granted a limited deviation allowing such contractors to compete; the subcommittee argued that outright exclusion could deter contractor cooperation needed to craft technical specifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Price or cost analysis thresholds for procurement
rubrics_metrics.description: Require formal price or cost analysis only above a practical threshold to avoid excessive time and expertise burdens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purchasing professionals suggested the analysis requirement be limited (e.g., equipment over $10,000) because competitive bidding often provides adequate price assurance for smaller purchases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objection to prior federal approval for sole source contracts at low thresholds
rubrics_metrics.description: Universities objected to a requirement that sole source procurements receive prior federal approval when the threshold is too low (e.g., $5,000).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requiring prior approvals for modest purchases was seen as impractical and burdensome; institutions favored higher thresholds or internal justification processes instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procurement documentation requirements for higher-value purchases
rubrics_metrics.description: For purchases above a specified dollar threshold (e.g., $10,000), institutions should document the basis for contractor selection, justification for lack of competition, and basis for the award price.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While documentation is important to prevent favoritism and ensure accountability, the subcommittee pushed for thresholds and language calibrated to institutional procurement realities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consultant reporting: defer reporting until post-award stage
rubrics_metrics.description: Report consultant use at post-award rather than at proposal stage where possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The subcommittee and some agency commenters argued consultants need not be reported pre-award, reducing administrative burden during proposal development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standardize on SF 269 and SF 272 for federal financial reporting (with Remarks allowance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should use standard federal financial reporting forms SF 269 and SF 272; A-110 permits agencies to use the 'Remarks' section for additional program-specific information if needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The NSF adopted SF 269/272, representing compromise and alignment with A-110 while allowing limited program-specific reporting via Remarks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial reporting frequency limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal agencies may not require financial reports more often than quarterly or less frequently than annually; a final report is required at project end.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This A-110 principle restricts agency demands for unduly frequent reporting and standardizes reporting frequency across agencies, subject to limited, justified deviations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal Cash Transaction Report timing should be reasonable (suggest 30 days)
rubrics_metrics.description: Deadlines for submitting the Federal Cash Transaction Report (previously 15 days) should be extended if necessary to reduce burden (e.g., to 30 days).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Warner requested an increase from 15 to 30 days to give institutional accounting offices reasonable time to assemble accurate cash transaction data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Records retention period (three years)
rubrics_metrics.description: Institutions should retain records for three years after closeout (as supported/adopted by NSF).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Three-year retention balances audit and accountability needs with institutional storage/management burdens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agencies should not add substantive requirements beyond A-110 without waiver or OMB approval
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal operating agencies should not impose additional requirements that exceed A-110 unless the deviation is formally requested and approved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The subcommittee resisted agency-specific regulations (e.g., DHEW/NIH attempts) that would reintroduce non-uniform requirements and argued for referral to GOGR/OMB before exceptions were implemented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal audit reports submitted only upon agency request
rubrics_metrics.description: Internal audit reports should not be routinely submitted to federal agencies; they should be provided only upon request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Warner opposed a DHEW requirement for routine internal audit report submission and suggested agencies request audits only when needed to avoid creating internal 'papermills' and protecting internal management confidentiality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define government property narrowly versus all property purchased with federal funds
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulation language should focus on 'government property' furnished to recipients rather than treating all property paid for with federal funds as government property.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Narrower definition reduces institutional accountability burdens for items essentially purchased and usable by the institution, aligning responsibility with practical stewardship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget revision approval thresholds (percentage and dollar limits)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sponsor approval thresholds for revised budgets should use balanced rules (e.g., 10 percent or $3,000, whichever is higher) rather than overly restrictive dollar/percentage triggers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frick recommended revising thresholds (from $10,000 or 10% down to 10% or $3,000) to better reflect institutional budgeting realities while maintaining sponsor oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow flexibility in basic research spending; avoid onerous interim financial reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Basic research projects need flexibility to reallocate funds as research evolves; quarterly or interim financial reports should not unduly constrain adaptive research spending.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters argued that requiring frequent reconciliations or early warnings on underexpenditures can encourage wasteful spending or constrain legitimate shifts in research focus; a final project financial report may be sufficient in many basic research contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit cost sharing paperwork and avoid requiring detailed cost-sharing ratios
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid imposing heavy cost-sharing reporting requirements (e.g., institutional/aggregate cost sharing ratios) that multiply paperwork without commensurate benefit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requiring detailed cost-sharing ratios across proposal, award, administration, and final report across hundreds of projects creates substantial administrative costs that may outweigh value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attachment G: agencies may request projected financial data but must justify burden
rubrics_metrics.description: Attachment G permits agencies to request additional financial reporting/forms, but such requests should be justified and crafted to minimize recipient burden.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The subcommittee engaged with NSF over projected financial data requests; the view was that if justified and kept reasonable, such data could be reported, but agencies should not use this as a blanket reason to increase reporting burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deviation/waiver process should be limited and based on compelling need
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies may seek deviations from A-110, but OMB should limit waiver approvals to unique and compelling situations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: GOGR praised OMB's limited waiver approvals and urged that deviations not become a backdoor to non-uniform requirements across agencies; exceptions should be narrowly granted and coordinated through OMB/COGR.
